risks.note: The commodity chemical space continues to experience pricing pressure due to excess global capacity and the availability of lower-priced imports from East Asia, particularly China, contributing to margin compression across several product segments.
Industry-wide margin pressures combined with cyclical demand conditions may continue to affect profitability until market demand and pricing conditions stabilise.

Dependence on petrochemical derivatives such as o-Xylene exposes the Company to feedstock price fluctuations; if cost increases cannot be passed through in pricing or offset through efficiency improvements, operating margins may be impacted.

risks.risk: Exposure to geopolitical and trade developments
risks.note: Global trade tensions, tariff actions and regional policy shifts may create uncertainty for the Company's export-oriented business, potentially affecting demand patterns and pricing stability.
Commodity chemical markets are inherently cyclical and closely linked to broader industry activity; periods of demand slowdown or pricing pressure may affect revenue visibility and profitability.

Operations depend on continuous, large-scale integrated manufacturing processes; the Company relies on Process Safety Management systems, periodic HAZOP studies, preventive maintenance and independent safety audits to manage operational and process-safety exposure across its facilities.

risks.risk: Higher financing burden from recent capital-intensive expansion
risks.note: Expansion projects undertaken in recent years, particularly at Dahej, have resulted in a higher capital base and increased financing requirements, which have impacted financial performance during the year pending improved utilisation levels.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A globally integrated specialty chemicals group and among the top-3 global manufacturers of Phthalic Anhydride, with an integrated industrial-and-food-grade manufacturing model spanning India, Malaysia and the United States.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Thirumalai Chemicals Limited manufactures and supplies commodity and specialty chemicals — Phthalic Anhydride, Maleic Anhydride, Malic Acid, Fumaric Acid and Diethyl Phthalate — from integrated manufacturing facilities in India (Ranipet, Tamil Nadu and Dahej, Gujarat), Malaysia (Kemaman) and, upon commissioning, the United States (West Virginia). Customers span plasticisers, resins (UPR), paints and coatings, pigments and dyes, food and beverages and pharmaceuticals across more than 60 countries.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's chemical demand structurally supported by construction, infrastructure, food and beverages, pharmaceuticals and consumer applications benefiting from the country's growth drivers and expanding consumption base
- Global speciality chemical market projected to grow from USD 5.56 billion in 2026 to USD 7.31 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 3.5%
- Demand for phthalic anhydride growing consistently on usage in plastics, coatings and automotive applications, with a 4-5% growth trajectory expected in UPR and paints across rapidly industrialising regions (Asia Pacific, Middle East, Latin America)
- India's chemicals and petrochemicals domestic demand expected to nearly triple to US$1 trillion by 2040, as global companies diversify supply chains away from China
- India-UK Free Trade Agreement (expected in force July 2026) expected to eliminate tariffs on 99% of Indian exports and reduce duties on 90% of UK exports to India, with the chemicals sector seen as a key beneficiary
- Aggressive pricing by low-cost producers, particularly in Asia, continues to compress margins across both commodity and specialty chemical segments, intensifying domestic and export competition
- Approximately 75% of Malic and Fumaric Acid consumed in the US currently relies on imports; American customers increasingly prioritising secure, domestic sourcing amid tariff and supply-chain risk, positioning the US subsidiary to capture market share
- Domestic PA market oversupply from aggressive competitor capacity additions is progressively being absorbed by underlying demand growth
- Sustainability (environmental compliance, energy efficiency) is described as now a competitive requirement rather than a differentiator for customers and regulators in global markets

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strategy continues to focus on areas where the Company possesses deep technical expertise and long-standing strengths, rather than aggressive diversification
- With major investments largely complete, focus is on maximising capacity utilisation, maintaining cost leadership and delivering consistent quality for value creation
- Expect improved operating leverage, stronger cash generation and gradual deleveraging of the balance sheet as Dahej reaches full contribution and the US project progresses
- In Malaysia (OOSB), disciplined cost management, calibrated production planning and strategic market realignment to strengthen competitiveness and protect margins amid China weakness and regional pricing pressure
- In Food Ingredients, proactively addressing import-dumping volatility by strengthening local distribution channels, shifting focus to high-yield segments, and leveraging lean operational frameworks
- Prioritising operational efficiency and cost discipline, with focus on yield improvement, energy optimisation and enhancing process reliability across manufacturing, in response to an operating landscape of subdued demand, tariff uncertainty, competitive pricing pressure, input cost volatility and rising sustainability expectations
- Organisational realignment initiatives to sharpen execution and improve operational responsiveness as the Company expands its presence across domestic and overseas markets, including systems to support overseas hiring and cross-border assignments
- This excerpt references a formal Dividend Distribution Policy and a Policy on Material Subsidiary, both disclosed via weblinks on the Company's website, but does not itself state the payout/reinvestment philosophy beyond pointing to those policies.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion in recent years has been the new Phthalic Anhydride facility at Dahej, Gujarat (within the PCPIR industrial cluster, Bharuch), commissioned under subsidiary TCL Intermediates Pvt. Ltd. to expand market footprint in western India; the facility has since been successfully commissioned and achieved 100% capacity utilisation after resolving initial stabilisation challenges, though it depends on imported Ortho-Xylene to mitigate domestic feedstock shortfalls. The larger ongoing project is a greenfield facility in West Virginia, United States, established through subsidiary TCL Specialties LLC to manufacture Maleic Anhydride, Malic Acid, Fumaric Acid and downstream derivatives for North American markets; fabrication is complete and pre-commissioning/startup activities are underway, though the project faced capital cost escalations from inflationary pressures, local labour shortages and extended regulatory equipment testing, and a debt-refinancing process (now handled by a newly engaged Debt Advisory Firm) is in progress to unlock full commercial operations. Existing capacity also includes the Optimistic Organic Sdn. Bhd. (OOSB) Maleic Anhydride unit in Kemaman, Malaysia, serving as a strategic hub for Asian markets. Separately, targeted investments in debottlenecking, automation and energy efficiency (including variable frequency drives, heat exchangers and condensate recovery systems) are described as ongoing initiatives to strengthen cost competitiveness across the manufacturing network.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 3rd largest global manufacturer of Phthalic Anhydride
- Largest producer of Maleic Anhydride in Southeast Asia
- Largest producer of Fumaric Acid in India, and the only manufacturer of Malic Acid in India
- Integrated manufacturing model spanning both industrial and food-grade production, enabling consistent quality, cost efficiencies and supply reliability
- Long-standing global customer relationships spanning decades across the Americas, Europe, Asia and the Middle East, including reputed clients such as Perfetti and Symrise
- Energy self-sufficiency: the PA plant is the primary energy hub generating power and steam for the integrated complex; more than 90% of PA operations' energy is derived from internally recovered process heat
- Zero Liquid Discharge systems at the Ranipet facility

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Competitive pricing and global oversupply — The commodity chemical space continues to experience pricing pressure due to excess global capacity and the availability of lower-priced imports from East Asia, particularly China, contributing to margin compression across several product segments.
- Persistent profitability pressures — Industry-wide margin pressures combined with cyclical demand conditions may continue to affect profitability until market demand and pricing conditions stabilise.
- Raw material price volatility — Dependence on petrochemical derivatives such as o-Xylene exposes the Company to feedstock price fluctuations; if cost increases cannot be passed through in pricing or offset through efficiency improvements, operating margins may be impacted.
- Exposure to geopolitical and trade developments — Global trade tensions, tariff actions and regional policy shifts may create uncertainty for the Company's export-oriented business, potentially affecting demand patterns and pricing stability.
- Structural commodity cycle vulnerability — Commodity chemical markets are inherently cyclical and closely linked to broader industry activity; periods of demand slowdown or pricing pressure may affect revenue visibility and profitability.
- Process safety and operational risk — Operations depend on continuous, large-scale integrated manufacturing processes; the Company relies on Process Safety Management systems, periodic HAZOP studies, preventive maintenance and independent safety audits to manage operational and process-safety exposure across its facilities.
- Higher financing burden from recent capital-intensive expansion — Expansion projects undertaken in recent years, particularly at Dahej, have resulted in a higher capital base and increased financing requirements, which have impacted financial performance during the year pending improved utilisation levels.
